name: Outworld Labs
long_description: Outworld Labs is building a simulation platform for training and evaluating robot foundation models. The platform is built on a brand new physics engine designed from the ground up for dexterous manipulation. It enables researchers to easily create realistic environments, reconstruct and augment real-world data, and improve their models through large-scale simulation without the cost of physical robots and real-world data collection.

launches.title: Outworld Labs: Simulation for training and evaluating robot foundation models
launches.body:
Hi! We’re Matei and Daniel, the founders of [Outworld Labs](https://outworldlabs.com/). We’re building a simulation platform for training and evaluating robot foundation models.

<https://youtu.be/mnklLUU5Bdk>

Collecting robot training data and testing models is expensive and difficult to scale. It requires physical robots, human operators, and repeated task setup and resets. Simulation could make both faster and cheaper, but inaccurate physics and limited environment diversity make it difficult to transfer simulated results to real robots. Complex and unintuitive tools also make setting up, scaling, and debugging simulations difficult.

We’re building Horizon to address these problems. At its core is a new physics engine designed from the ground up for dexterous manipulation. Alongside it, we’re building tools to create realistic environments, reconstruct and augment real-world data, and run simulation, training, and evaluation workloads at scale—all in one platform.

Our goal is to help robotics teams generate more diverse training data and reliably evaluate models across tasks, objects, and environments, with less reliance on physical robots and manual data collection.

We met during our master’s in EECS at UC Berkeley. If you’re building robot foundation models or working on robot training and evaluation, we’d love to hear about your workflow and explore how we could help.
